newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan current account surplus down 28.9 pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Japan current account surplus down 28.9 pct in Aug.

text.p: The surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, shrank 28.9 percent to 460.60 billion yen in August from a year earlier, the Finance Ministry announced on Wednesday.
The surplus in merchandise trade alone decreased by 27.8 percent to 566.70 billion yen from the same month a year earlier, dropping year-on-year for the 21st straight month.
The August current account surplus was in line with economists' forecasts, which showed that on average, they expected a year-on-year fall of 28 percent in the figure.

Economists had said that a continuing flow of imports into Japan was pushing down the nation's overall current account surplus. Japan's current account surplus has been on a declining trend since September 1995.

But they said the pace of the drop is slowing, as the yen is weaker than it was the previous year. A weak yen makes foreign products less competitive in Japanese markets because it inflates their prices in yen terms.
A deficit in the service account, especially the transport and travel accounts, was expected to have increased in August.
